pr_title: Serialize output caching entries to binary

issue_context.title: Use custom binary serialization for output cache entries
issue_context.body:
Current using JSON serialization, which is slower and uses more space. Since the serialized entity is well-known, we could use the same logic that is used for sessions.

Reference implementation for sessions: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/df445e5031e2a39ea4802e949b82a7946eb9ce79/src/Middleware/Session/src/DistributedSession.cs
comments:
Structure to serialize:

```c#
internal sealed class FormatterEntry
{
    public DateTimeOffset Created { get; set; }
    public int StatusCode { get; set; }
    public Dictionary<string, string?[]> Headers { get; set; } = default!;
    public List<byte[]> Body { get; set; } = default!;
    public string[] Tags { get; set; } = default!;
}
```

Suggested format:

```
Serialization revision:
  7-bit encoded int
Creation date:
  Ticks: 7-bit encoded long
  Offset.TotalMinutes: 7-bit encoded long
Status code:
  7-bit encoded int
Headers:
  Headers count: 7-bit encoded int
  For each header:
    key name byte length: 7-bit encoded int
    UTF-8 encoded key name byte[]
    Values count: 7-bit encoded int
    For each header value:
      data byte length: 7-bit encoded int
      UTF-8 encoded byte[]
Body:
  Segments count: 7-bit encoded int
  For each segment:
    data byte length: 7-bit encoded int
    data byte[]
Tags:
  Tags count: 7-bit encoded int
  For each tag:
    data byte length: 7-bit encoded int
    UTF-8 encoded byte[]
```

You also need to account for adding more entries in the future. Also, we need to support mix deployments with old and new versions running concurrent. The schema needs to be designed in such a way that old and new versions of asp.net can gracefully read these cache entries without blowing up.

review_comments:
There's allocations for the MemoryStream and the BinaryWriter. Should these be cached / pooled?

(similar for Deserialize)

I don't think these should be pooled, they don't have reusable state. Ideally we should use a custom `MemoryStream` that pools its buffers (there is an issue for that in the runtime). Or change the API design such that we can use streams with the cache store instead of returning `byte[]`.
Should this write 0 still? Otherwise the reader will try to read the length but get the next thing written which could be the next header key length or the body count.

Right, also wondering if the value can be null at all in a request. I think I can force it by code, but what would be the value of "header1: ", I would assume `string.Empty` but not null. And assuming we write a length of `0`, should we deserialize it with `""` or `null`.

My preference is to deserialize it as `""` in that case.

Well in this case just write 0 for the length.

In the other two cases set value to string.Empty and let `BinaryWriter.Write(string)` handle it.
